question: U9 B1 split, predictions pushed first: in CAP-U9REST.json B1 the capture scrolled the selected Shape 973 px out of view and then pressed a Button in the next section; the Shape read unselected and an Add Section faded in. Which did it: the scroll alone, or the press alone?
setup: Gestures Probe, unsaved, window 1600 by 1400, B's build from CAP-U9REST.json (two sections, a Button and a moved Shape in section 0, a Button in section 1). S: frame at 0, select the Shape, then the frame scrolled 973 px (as the tool's scroll in B1), no pointer event, read 0.9 s later. P: frame at 120 so both blocks sit clear of the tool's 150 px scroll margin, select the Shape, press the Button in section 1 with no scroll, 2 px, let go. Each built twice in this capture, Exit Without Saving between.
bet: The scroll alone. CAP-U9REST2.json and CAP-U9REST3.json (fresh) read that with one block selected, a press and 2 px in another section change nothing until the let go.

predictions.predict: Shape unselected; an Add Section fades in within about 0.35 s (S add, recorded, not scored).
Shape still selected; Button not selected.
Shape unselected, Button selected. No Add Section fades during the press (P add, recorded, not scored).

outcomes: Scroll alone: S scrolled unselected, P as predicted. Press alone: S scrolled still selected, P pressed unselected. Neither alone (it takes both): S scrolled selected and P pressed selected.
scoring: data-is-selected of each read, each case only if its two reads agree. The fade watches are recorded and reported, not scored.
